headline: Take-Two drops 4.4% last night on GTA 6 jitters while Labor pushes ahead with CGT reform — a busy day for your portfolio and the news feed.

portfolio.summary: The big mover last night was Take-Two Interactive (TTWO), down 4.4% — the sharpest fall in the portfolio. Google also slipped 1.2%, while everything else was pretty quiet. On the ASX today, your holdings barely budged — CBA ticked up a cent, VGE edged slightly higher, and the rest drifted fractionally lower.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Dropped $10.53 to $227.55 last night. No major company-specific news broke — GTA 6 collector's edition pre-order speculation is circling, but the market appears nervous about the game's release timeline and valuation. Worth watching ahead of any release date confirmation.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: Fell $4.69 to $382.97 last night. The dip came despite recent strong earnings — Google also unveiled a major new AI model (Gemini Omni) overnight, but the market didn't reward it. Could be profit-taking after a strong run.

movers.name: BetaShares Global Energy ETF
movers.note: Slipped 6 cents to $8.80 at today's close. OPEC has cut its global oil demand growth forecast for 2026, which puts mild downward pressure on energy stocks globally.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: Down $1.58 to $515.48 at today's ASX close, tracking last night's mild US market softness. Not alarming — the S&P 500 and NASDAQ were actually slightly positive last night, so this likely reflects currency and timing effects.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: Up 21 cents to $92.59 today — a quiet positive session. The rising Aussie dollar (now 71.7 US cents) can sometimes weigh on unhedged international ETFs, but VGE held up fine.

movers.name: Commonwealth Bank of Australia
movers.note: Essentially flat at $164.64 today — up just 4 cents. No news driving it. CBA continues to trade at elevated levels; nothing to act on today.

markets.summary: Last night's US session was mildly positive — the S&P 500 gained 0.37% and the NASDAQ edged up 0.19%, so the broader mood in the US was fine. The ASX 200 pulled back 0.4% today to close at 8,657, giving back some recent gains. Oil is steady just under $97 a barrel, gold eased slightly to $4,521/oz, and the Australian dollar is a little stronger at about 71.7 US cents.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Pulled back slightly today after recent gains. No single big driver — broad, mild profit-taking.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Last night's session was quietly positive. Markets shrugged off mixed signals and drifted higher.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: Small gain last night despite weakness in a few big-name tech stocks including Google.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Holding near $97 — OPEC demand forecast cuts offset by supply concerns keeping the floor in.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Eased slightly but still at very elevated levels historically. No major catalyst today.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: The Aussie dollar ticked up — traders are backing away from bets that the RBA will keep hiking rates aggressively, which paradoxically boosted the currency as bond markets settled.

politics.summary: A big day for tax and housing policy — Labor is pushing ahead with plans to link personal tax cuts to capital gains tax (CGT) and negative gearing changes, and it's ignoring calls to pause. There's also a solo voice demanding the Reserve Bank hike rates again, going against the current consensus.

stories.title: Labor ties $4,500 tax cuts to CGT and negative gearing changes
stories.why_it_matters: Labor wants to fund personal income tax cuts — reportedly around $4,500 for workers earning under $135k — by raising the capital gains tax (CGT) discount from 50% down to 25%, and tightening negative gearing rules on existing investment properties. In plain English: if you sell an investment property or shares you've held for over a year, you'd pay tax on a bigger portion of the profit. Property investors and landlords are the biggest losers here. The government is ignoring calls from industry groups to pause the reforms. If you own investment property or have large unrealised capital gains, this is worth tracking closely.

stories.title: Expert bucks the trend and calls for RBA to hike interest rates
stories.why_it_matters: While the consensus among economists is that the RBA (Reserve Bank of Australia — the body that sets interest rates) is done hiking, at least one prominent expert is publicly calling for another rate rise. This is a minority view right now — the AFR reported that bets on more RBA hikes are actually unwinding, and demand for Australian government bonds is rising (meaning investors think rates are heading lower, not higher). For borrowers and property holders, the base case remains that rates have peaked, but the debate isn't completely closed.

stories.title: AUD rising even as RBA rate hike bets fade — here's why
stories.why_it_matters: Normally you'd expect the Aussie dollar to fall when markets think the RBA won't raise rates — because higher rates attract foreign money seeking better returns. But the AUD is actually rising today (to about 71.7 US cents), partly because global investors are feeling more confident generally, and partly because fears about Australian government debt are easing. A stronger AUD is a mild headwind for your unhedged international holdings (like VTS and GOOGL) because overseas gains are worth slightly less when converted back to Aussie dollars.

ai.summary: Two big AI stories today: Google has launched a major new model called Gemini Omni, and Pope Leo has made global headlines by releasing a formal document calling for tough regulation of AI — specifically flagging that some autonomous weapons are already beyond human control.

stories.title: Google launches Gemini Omni — its most capable AI model yet
stories.why_it_matters: Google has officially unveiled Gemini Omni, described as its most powerful AI model to date. The name 'Omni' signals it can handle text, images, audio and more in a single system — what the industry calls multimodal (meaning it works across multiple types of content at once, not just text). This is directly relevant to your GOOGL holding: it's Google's answer to OpenAI's GPT-4o and shows the company is still pushing hard in the AI race. The stock dipped 1.2% last night despite this news, possibly because investors expected even more, or are simply taking profits after a strong earnings-driven run.

stories.title: Pope Leo issues landmark document calling for global AI regulation
stories.why_it_matters: Pope Leo has released what's being called a formal teaching document — essentially an official Catholic Church position paper — focused on AI and the future of humanity. The headline warning: some autonomous weapons systems (think AI-controlled drones or missiles) have already reached a point where no human can meaningfully control or recall them. He's calling on world governments to establish binding international regulations on AI development, particularly in military applications. It's not just a religious statement — it's entering the same conversation as the EU AI Act and US executive orders, and signals growing pressure on big tech companies (including Google and Microsoft) to accept more regulatory oversight.

sport.summary: AFL is mourning the passing of Neale Daniher, a legend of the game who spent years fighting MND. NRL Round 13 is shaping up with significant injury news for the Warriors and Tigers. And a World Surf League event in New Zealand has been suspended after a scary incident involving an Australian photographer.

stories.title: AFL legend and MND warrior Neale Daniher passes away
stories.why_it_matters: Neale Daniher, the former Melbourne Demons coach and one of the most beloved figures in Australian football, has died after his long battle with MND (Motor Neurone Disease — a devastating illness that progressively shuts down the body's ability to move and breathe). Daniher had spent years as one of the most prominent advocates and fundraisers for MND research, helping raise tens of millions of dollars through the Big Freeze campaign at the MCG. Garry Lyon led tributes and has called on Prime Minister Anthony Albanese to act on MND funding in Daniher's honour. A genuine giant of the game, on and off the field.

stories.title: NRL Round 13: Warriors and Tigers hit hard by injury news
stories.why_it_matters: Heading into Round 13, both the Warriors and the Tigers have copped serious injury blows. The Warriors have confirmed Mitchell Barnett is out (knee), while Fox Sports reports that another key Warriors player has described his injury as 'my footy done' — suggesting a season-ending blow. The Tigers are without Jahream Bula (suspended). There's also intrigue around the Moses situation (reported as a 'stunning twist') and uncertainty about which State of Origin players will be available for their clubs this week. If you're playing NRL Fantasy, check your squads carefully before lockout.

stories.title: World Surf League event in NZ suspended after Australian photographer bitten in water
stories.why_it_matters: A World Surf League competition in New Zealand has been put on hold after an Australian photographer was bitten while in the water — reports suggest it was either a shark or a sea lion, with authorities still investigating. The photographer was treated for injuries, and the WSL immediately suspended the event as a precaution. It's a reminder of the real risks in open-water surf contests, and organisers are waiting on official confirmation of what caused the bite before deciding whether to resume competition.

watch_today.title: TTWO: Significant drop — hold but keep a close eye
watch_today.detail: Take-Two fell 4.4% last night to $227.55, the biggest single-day move in your portfolio. There's no confirmed bad news — GTA 6 speculation continues and collector's edition pre-orders are being discussed, which is actually a positive signal. But the stock is volatile and any delay announcement for GTA 6 could hit it hard. Stay put for now, but watch for any official release date news from Rockstar/Take-Two this week.

watch_today.title: GOOGL: Gemini Omni launch didn't lift the stock — monitor closely
watch_today.detail: Google launched its biggest AI model yet (Gemini Omni) overnight, but the stock still fell 1.2% to $382.97. When good news doesn't move a stock higher, it can signal the market has already priced in the optimism — or that investors want to see real revenue from AI tools, not just announcements. Nothing to sell on, but worth watching how the market reacts to Gemini Omni over the coming days.

watch_today.title: Labor's CGT reform: property investors and those with large capital gains should pay attention
watch_today.detail: Labor is pushing ahead with plans to cut the CGT discount (the tax break you get when selling assets held over 12 months) from 50% down to 25%, and tighten negative gearing on existing properties. If you have investment properties or large unrealised gains in shares, now is a good time to talk to your accountant about the timing of any potential sales. Nothing is law yet, but the government is clearly serious about this.

watch_today.title: FUEL.AX: OPEC demand cut is a mild headwind, oil still holding near $97
watch_today.detail: OPEC has trimmed its 2026 global oil demand growth forecast, which is a soft negative for energy ETFs like FUEL. That said, oil is still sitting near $96.60/barrel and supply concerns are keeping the price supported. No reason to sell — just be aware the macro tailwind for energy stocks is getting a little less strong.

watch_today.title: AUD at 71.7c — mild drag on unhedged international holdings
watch_today.detail: The Aussie dollar has ticked up today, which is generally good news for your cost of living but is a small headwind for your unhedged overseas holdings (GOOGL, MSFT, TTWO, VTS, VDHG). Gains those assets make in USD are worth slightly less when converted back to AUD. Nothing dramatic — just worth keeping in mind if the AUD keeps climbing.
